summary: Study packet with 4 key ideas, 8 practice questions with an answer key, and 6 glossary terms. Each answer shows the line it came from.

keyIdeas.title: How Plants Make Their Food
keyIdeas.explanation: Plants use a process called photosynthesis to turn light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar. This happens inside tiny green structures called chloroplasts in the leaves.
keyIdeas.quote: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to turn light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.

keyIdeas.title: What Goes In and What Comes Out
keyIdeas.explanation: Plants need light, water, and carbon dioxide to make glucose and oxygen. The roots take up water, and carbon dioxide enters through small openings called stomata.
keyIdeas.quote: A plant needs three things for photosynthesis: light, water and carbon dioxide.

keyIdeas.title: The Two Stages
keyIdeas.explanation: Photosynthesis happens in two stages: the light reactions and the Calvin cycle. The light reactions split water to release oxygen and make energy molecules, while the Calvin cycle turns carbon dioxide into sugar.
keyIdeas.quote: Photosynthesis happens in two connected stages.

keyIdeas.title: Factors affecting speed
keyIdeas.explanation: Three main things change how fast photosynthesis runs: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature. Very high temperatures slow the process because enzymes stop working properly above about 40 degrees Celsius.
keyIdeas.quote: [22] Three main factors change how fast photosynthesis runs: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature.

questions.question: What is the process that plants use to turn light energy into chemical energy?
questions.quote: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to turn light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.

questions.question: Where does photosynthesis happen mainly?
questions.quote: It happens mainly in the leaves, inside tiny green structures called chloroplasts.

questions.question: What three things does a plant need for photosynthesis?
questions.quote: A plant needs three things for photosynthesis: light, water and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Through what do carbon dioxide molecules enter the leaf from the air?
questions.quote: Carbon dioxide enters the leaf from the air through small openings called stomata.

questions.question: What are the three main factors that change how fast photosynthesis runs?
questions.answer: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature
questions.quote: [22] Three main factors change how fast photosynthesis runs: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature.

questions.question: What happens to photosynthesis when the weather is hot and dry?
questions.answer: the stomata close to save water, which also cuts off the supply of carbon dioxide
questions.quote: [22] When the weather is hot and dry, the stomata close to save water, which also cuts off the supply of carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Why do scientists study photosynthesis so closely?
questions.answer: burning fossil fuels and cutting down forests both reduce the amount of carbon dioxide that plants and algae can absorb
questions.quote: [25] Burning fossil fuels and cutting down forests both reduce the amount of carbon dioxide that plants and algae can absorb, which is one reason scientists study photosynthesis so closely.

questions.question: What comes from photosynthesis that is almost all in the air?
questions.quote: [25] Almost all the oxygen in the air comes from photosynthesis, and almost all the food eaten by animals starts as sugar made by plants, algae or some bacteria.

glossary.definition: tiny green structures inside leaves where photosynthesis happens
glossary.quote: It happens mainly in the leaves, inside tiny green structures called chloroplasts.

glossary.definition: a pigment found inside chloroplasts that gives leaves their green colour
glossary.quote: The green colour of leaves comes from chlorophyll, a pigment found inside the chloroplasts.

glossary.definition: narrow tubes that carry water from the roots up to the leaves
glossary.quote: The roots take up water from the soil, and the water travels up to the leaves through narrow tubes called xylem.

glossary.definition: parts that close to save water when the weather is hot and dry
glossary.quote: [22] When the weather is hot and dry, the stomata close to save water, which also cuts off the supply of carbon dioxide.

glossary.definition: RuBisCO is an example of an enzyme that stops working properly above about 40 degrees Celsius
glossary.quote: [22] Very high temperatures slow it down because enzymes such as RuBisCO stop working properly above about 40 degrees Celsius.

glossary.definition: things that, when burned, reduce the amount of carbon dioxide that plants and algae can absorb
glossary.quote: [25] Burning fossil fuels and cutting down forests both reduce the amount of carbon dioxide that plants and algae can absorb, which is one reason scientists study photosynthesis so closely.
